tool: py-spy 0.4.2 record --nonblocking --rate 50 --duration 90 + read-only SQL probes on the live bed
question: Is FTS5 segment-merge amplification the serial-writer hot path behind the ingest throughput decay?
verdict: NO — refuted. FTS5 is 0.07% of writer wall time. The decay is auto_link_by_entity (entity-graph COVER-edge formation): 89.5% of writer wall time, O(hub-posting-list) per insert, O(N^2) per build. Second-order: unindexed filename_index DELETE (6.6%, also O(N) per insert).

live_query_probe.note: auto_link_by_entity's exact SQL, run read-only against the live bed with the newest gene's 15 entities
live_query_probe.plan: SEARCH entity_graph USING COVERING INDEX (entity=?); USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY; USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
live_query_probe.filename_index_delete_plan: SCAN filename_index (no gene_id index; 278,902 rows at probe time)

decay_curve.note: instantaneous genes/s over ~10k-gene windows from the 18:07 build log; rate*N ~ constant (~2.0e6 -> 1.85e6) from 136k on = O(N^2) signature. Rise to 61 g/s through the EnronQA core (low hub density, tagging-bound), collapse once padding-root MIME hubs accumulate.
decay_curve.projection_status_quo: ~670k total genes expected (517,353 files x 1.296 genes/file); remaining (670k^2-322k^2)/(2*1.85e6) ~ 93,000 s ~ 26 h
decay_curve.projection_with_fix: writer residual ~4% of current per-insert cost -> tagging-bound again (~50 g/s with 6 workers); remaining ~348k genes ~ 2 h

fts5_answers.a_automerge_tuning: Moot at this scale: genes_fts_config holds only version=4 (pure defaults: automerge=4, usermerge=4, crisismerge=16); segment tree healthy at probe time (23 segments, 9 levels, one level-4 merge in flight, 117,662 index pages ~ 460MB); total FTS share of writer wall time 0.07% (3/4352 samples). Tuning or periodic explicit merges could recover at most that.
fts5_answers.b_defer_fts_population: Not the win: at most 0.07% today. Rebuild machinery exists if ever needed (external-content 'rebuild' command, storage/ddl.py:485-529). Deferral only becomes worth re-profiling after the entity-autolink and filename-index fixes, on a bed 5-10x this size.
fts5_answers.c_contentless_external_content: Already shipped: genes_fts has been the external-content form since issue #338 (no genes_fts_content shadow table in the live bed) — insert cost is tokenize + level-0 write only, which is what the 0.07% measures.

fixes.idx_filename_gene: filename_anchor.ensure_schema now creates idx_filename_gene ON filename_index(gene_id). Content-neutral (an index changes no query results); existing beds pick it up on next open. Kills the 6.6% O(N) DELETE scan.
fixes.entity_autolink_knob: KnowledgeStore(entity_autolink=False) / build_fixture_matrix --no-entity-autolink / CYMATIX_BFM_ENTITY_AUTOLINK=0 skips per-insert COVER-edge formation; entity_graph rows still written. documents+content+entity-row digests byte-identical (see entity_autolink_equivalence_enronqa.json); the only delta is gene_relations relation=5 edges, which are default-inert at query time (W2.1 cover-walk kill, ladder_v09x_w2_cover_walk_2026-08-28.json) and already order-nondeterministic under --parallel (ingest_equivalence_enronqa.json: 8675 vs 8664).

not_fixed_here.auto_link_hub_cutoff: A posting-count cutoff in auto_link_by_entity (PKI_NOISE_CUTOFF precedent, storage/indexes.py) would bound per-insert cost for ingest paths that keep linking ON — but it changes which edges form, so it needs its own receipt + issue, not a scheduling change.
not_fixed_here.tagger_mime_header_entities: 'content-type'/'content-transfer-encoding'/'mime-version'/'x-origin' as extracted entities are MIME plumbing, not entities; multi-line garbage entities also observed ('john martin - baylor\ncc: ...'). Fixing the CPU tagger changes gene tags = bed content; out of scope for a scheduling fix.
